subject: Computer Networking
title: Mobile Network Privacy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mobile Network Privacy.

hook.text: Your phone reveals your location to cell towers constantly. That data tells a detailed story about your life.

buildup.text: Carriers know which towers you connect to and when. That creates a precise log of your movements.

discovery.text: IMSI catchers — fake cell towers — trick your phone into connecting. Law enforcement and hackers both use them.

twist.text: 5G improved subscriber privacy with SUPI encryption. Your identity is hidden from eavesdroppers on the radio link.

climax.text: VPNs protect your data but not your location. Only airplane mode truly stops your phone from broadcasting its position.

punchline.text: Your phone is a tracking device you carry willingly.

quiz.question: What is an IMSI catcher?
options: A fake cell tower that tricks phones into connecting
A tool that measures internet speed
A device that blocks all wireless signals

details.summary: Mobile networks expose users to privacy risks including carrier tracking, cell tower location data, IMSI catchers that impersonate towers, and deep packet inspection. Carriers can see metadata about all connections.
details.whyItMatters: Phones constantly communicate with cell towers, creating a detailed location history. Understanding mobile privacy risks helps users make informed decisions about protecting their communications.
takeaways: Cell towers inherently track phone locations continuously
IMSI catchers impersonate towers to intercept communications
5G encrypts subscriber identifiers that 4G transmitted in plaintext

faq.question: What is an IMSI catcher?
faq.answer: An IMSI catcher is a device that impersonates a cell tower, tricking phones into connecting to it. This exposes the phone's IMSI identity number and can intercept calls and texts. Law enforcement uses them for surveillance. Criminals use them for eavesdropping.

faq.question: Can a VPN protect mobile privacy?
faq.answer: A VPN encrypts data content so the carrier cannot inspect it, hiding which websites you visit. However, the carrier still sees that you are connected and your location from cell tower connections.
